title: Lemon Bundt Cake with Lemon Glaze
changes_from_base: Lemon zest soaked in juice and buttermilk replace the soured cream and most of the vanilla; lemon-juice glaze.
summary: This follows the classic vanilla Bundt method, but swaps the soured cream for buttermilk and loads the batter with lemon zest and juice, finishing with a sharp lemon glaze. A tender, fragrant ring cake that slices beautifully for a crowd.
equipment: stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt, or table salt
unsalted butter, softened (about 18°C), plus extra for the tin

steps.title: Heat oven, prepare tin
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan) for at least 20 minutes with a shelf in the lower-middle position. Brush every ridge of the Bundt tin with soft butter, dust with the 15 g flour and tap out the excess. A thorough coating in each groove is what lets the cake release cleanly, with all its sharp ridges intact.

steps.title: Soak the zest
steps.text: Mix the lemon zest with the 3 tbsp lemon juice and leave for 10-15 minutes. The juice softens the zest so it spreads evenly through the batter and releases more of its fragrant oils.

steps.title: Ready the dry and wet
steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and salt together. Stir the zest mixture and vanilla into the buttermilk; it may thicken slightly, which is fine. Lightly beat the eggs with the extra yolk in a separate jug.

steps.title: Cream butter and sugar
steps.text: Beat the butter and caster sugar for 3-4 minutes until pale and fluffy, then add the eggs in 2 parts, scraping down the bowl each time. Creaming whips tiny air bubbles into the butter, which the raising agents then expand in the oven for a light, even crumb.

steps.title: Alternate flour and buttermilk
steps.text: With the mixer on low, add the flour mixture in 3 parts, alternating with the lemon buttermilk in 2, and mix just until smooth. Adding them in turns keeps the batter from splitting, and stopping as soon as it is smooth avoids developing gluten that would make the cake tough.

steps.title: Fill and bake
steps.text: Spoon the batter into the tin, level the top and tap the tin firmly on the worktop to knock out large air pockets. Bake for 45-55 minutes until golden, springy to the touch and a skewer pushed into the thickest part comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool and turn out
steps.text: Leave the cake in the tin for 10 minutes, then invert it onto the wire rack and cool for at least 2 hours. Those first minutes let the crumb firm up enough to hold together, while turning it out before it is cold stops steam from making it stick.

steps.title: Glaze the cake
steps.text: Whisk the icing sugar with the 2 tbsp lemon juice and the buttermilk until thick but pourable, adding extra lemon juice drop by drop if needed. Spoon it over the cold cake so it runs down the ridges, then leave for 25 minutes to set.

tips: Leave the lemon zest to soak in the juice and buttermilk for a few minutes before mixing, so its fragrant oils flavour the whole cake.
A common mistake is greasing the tin carelessly; any bare patch in the ridges can tear the cake, so brush butter into every groove before flouring.
Grate only the yellow zest, not the bitter white pith underneath.
Bring the eggs and buttermilk to room temperature so they blend smoothly into the creamed butter without curdling.
Make sure the cake is completely cold before glazing, or the glaze will melt and soak in rather than setting in neat drips.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. The unglazed cake can be wrapped well and frozen for up to 2 months; thaw at room temperature and glaze before serving.
